title: Visibility timeout, retries, and Dead Letter Queues (DLQ)
hook: When a consumer receives an SQS message, it becomes invisible to other consumers for the visibility timeout. If processing fails or takes too long, the message reappears — or after too many attempts, lands in a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) for inspection.

blocks.text: Visibility timeout is the interval during which a received message is hidden from other pollers. Successful processing ends with DeleteMessage. Failure without delete causes redelivery after timeout. A redrive policy moves messages to a DLQ after maxReceiveCount failed receives. DLQs isolate poison messages so the main queue keeps flowing.

entries.plainDefinition: Seconds a message is hidden after ReceiveMessage.
entries.example: 60 seconds — handler must finish or extend visibility.

entries.plainDefinition: Queue holding messages that exceeded max receive attempts.
entries.example: orders-dlq receives malformed JSON after 3 failures.

entries.plainDefinition: Redrive threshold before message moves to DLQ.
entries.example: 3 — third failed receive triggers DLQ move.

entries.plainDefinition: Moving messages from DLQ back to source queue after fix.

blocks.text: Visibility timeout shorter than handler duration causes duplicate processing — the classic SQS bug. No DLQ means poison messages retry forever, inflating queue depth and costs. Senior engineers alarm on DLQ depth and set visibility to roughly 6× Lambda timeout per AWS guidance.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: visibility hides in-flight work. Too short = duplicates. maxReceiveCount + DLQ = circuit breaker for poison pills.

items.body: Success → DeleteMessage. Failure → do not delete.

items.title: Exceed maxReceiveCount

stateDiagram-v2

snippet.label: CloudFormation — main queue with DLQ redrive
snippet.code:
Resources:
  OrdersDLQ:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties:
      QueueName: orders-dlq
  OrdersQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties:
      QueueName: orders
      VisibilityTimeout: 180
      RedrivePolicy:
        deadLetterTargetArn: !GetAtt OrdersDLQ.Arn
        maxReceiveCount: 3
snippet.explanation: RedrivePolicy links DLQ. VisibilityTimeout 180 suits Lambda with 30s timeout × 6 rule of thumb.

snippet.label: CLI — extend visibility during long processing
snippet.explanation: Call periodically for jobs longer than initial visibility. Receipt handle invalid after delete or timeout expiry.

snippet.label: TypeScript — heartbeat visibility extension
snippet.explanation: Pattern for EC2/ECS workers with variable duration. Lambda usually sets visibility via event source mapping instead.

snippet.label: CLI — redrive DLQ messages after fix
snippet.explanation: DLQ redrive API replays after root cause fixed. Throttle rate to avoid overwhelming consumers.

blocks.title: SQS visibility versus BullMQ stalled jobs
Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Visibility timeout 30s with 5-minute Lambda. No DLQ on production queues. maxReceiveCount 100 — delays poison detection. Deleting message before work commits to database — message lost on crash after delete.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: plot ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible alongside Errors — rising invisible count with duplicates in DB confirms visibility misconfiguration. DLQ alarm threshold ≥ 1 message for payment queues. Inspect ApproximateReceiveCount on sample messages before redrive.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: No retry on crash after delete

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'set visibility to same as Lambda timeout.' Strong answer: 6× Lambda timeout or heartbeat extension; delete only after idempotent commit.

interviewTakeaways: Visibility timeout hides in-flight messages; shorter than handler duration causes duplicates.
DLQ + maxReceiveCount isolates poison messages — alarm DLQ depth in production.
Delete message only after durable commit; extend visibility for long jobs.
60s: Visibility 6× handler. DLQ after 3 receives. Alarm DLQ. Redrive after fix not before.
Follow-up: how does Lambda event source mapping set visibility automatically?
commonPitfalls: Visibility 30s with 2-minute handler — classic duplicate charge scenario.
Strong answer: 6× timeout or ChangeMessageVisibility heartbeat during processing.
No DLQ — poison message retries forever inflating costs.
Deleting message before database transaction commits — data loss on crash.

jsTsCorrelations.note: C# Polly retry policies on SQS receive map to manual re-queue with DelaySeconds — similar to BackgroundService catch block with exponential backoff before rethrow.
RabbitMQ nack requeue resembles not deleting SQS message; DLQ is like dead-letter exchange after max retries.
